issues.t: Engine knocking or sudden engine failure (rod bearings)
issues.sym: A deep knock from the engine that gets louder with speed, a flashing check engine light or low oil pressure warning, and in the worst cases the engine stops and won't restart.
issues.why: Owners of both engines report connecting-rod bearing failures, usually around 90,000 to 115,000 miles. Low oil level, long oil-change intervals and oil-pressure problems are the usual suspects. The Genesis Coupe was not part of Hyundai's engine-bearing recalls for other models.
issues.next: If you hear a new knock, pull over and shut the engine off; driving on a failing bearing destroys the engine. Check the oil level, have it towed, and ask Hyundai whether any goodwill help applies to your VIN.

issues.t: Timing chain or cam timing faults (P0014, P0017)
issues.sym: Check engine light with timing codes such as P0014 or P0017, rough running, a rattle from the front of the engine, or a crank-but-no-start.
issues.why: On the turbo 4-cylinder, the variable cam timing units (CVVT) and timing chain parts can stick or wear, letting cam timing drift out of spec. Owners report chains, tensioners, guides and CVVT gears being replaced from about 30,000 miles on. Old or low oil makes it worse.
issues.next: Get the codes read soon and check the oil level. Don't keep driving with a timing rattle; a jumped chain can bend valves and turn a timing job into an engine rebuild.

issues.t: Timing chain rattle on cold start
issues.sym: A rattle or chatter for a few seconds after a cold start that fades once the engine warms up.
issues.why: On the 2013-2016 direct-injection V6, the timing chain tensioners, guides and cam phasers wear. Owners call it the most common weak spot of this engine.
issues.next: Have a shop listen to it and check for cam timing codes. Fixing it early (chain, guides, tensioners and phasers) can prevent damage from a chain that jumps.

issues.t: Misfires and rough idle from intake valve carbon
issues.sym: Rough idle, hesitation, reduced throttle response and a check engine light for misfires, usually from about 60,000 to 90,000 miles.
issues.why: This V6 sprays fuel straight into the cylinders, so nothing washes the backs of the intake valves. Oil vapor bakes onto them and builds carbon that disturbs airflow.
issues.next: Have a shop confirm misfires are not from plugs or coils first. If carbon is the cause, a walnut-blast cleaning of the intake valves usually fixes it.

issues.t: Unstable idle or stalling from a dirty throttle body
issues.sym: Idle that hunts up and down, stalls, a sudden cut in throttle, or a check engine light with codes like P050A (cold-start idle control).
issues.why: Carbon deposits build up between the throttle plate and its bore, so the computer can't control idle airflow properly. Hyundai issued a bulletin on cleaning these deposits, and some cars also needed computer updates.
issues.next: Ask a shop to clean the throttle body and check for software updates. If the problem keeps coming back, the throttle body or engine computer may need replacing.

issues.t: Turbo loses boost or wastegate actuator breaks
issues.sym: Sudden loss of power, an overboost or underboost code, or a rattle from the turbo area.
issues.why: Owners report the turbo's wastegate actuator arm breaking or the boost control valve failing, sometimes at low mileage. Turbo bolts or manifold studs can also snap when the turbo is removed.
issues.next: Ease off and avoid full throttle until it's checked; an uncontrolled turbo can damage the engine. Have a shop read the codes and inspect the wastegate linkage and boost control valve.

issues.t: Oil leak from the turbo oil feed line
issues.sym: Oil drips under the front of the car, a burning-oil smell after driving, or oil wetting the turbo area.
issues.why: The braided oil line that feeds the turbo can seep at its crimped end or at the banjo bolt threads.
issues.next: Have the leak traced and the line replaced. Oil dripping on a hot turbo can smoke or catch fire, so don't ignore it.

issues.t: Engine revs hang between gear shifts
issues.sym: When you lift off the gas to shift, the engine speed falls slowly, making smooth manual shifts hard and causing the car to lurch.
issues.why: The engine computer's original programming held revs up when the throttle closed. Hyundai released a computer update for slow RPM drop on throttle release.
issues.next: Ask a Hyundai dealer to check that the latest engine software is installed.

issues.t: Manual transmission grinds between gears
issues.sym: Grinding going into a gear (often 2nd, 3rd or 5th), notchy shifts, or a gear that is hard to get into, especially when the transmission is cold or you shift fast.
issues.why: The synchronizers that match gear speeds wear or were weak from new. Hyundai issued campaigns early on to replace the shift lever and change the gear oil, and some cars got replacement transmissions under warranty.
issues.next: Ask a dealer whether the shift lever and fluid campaigns were done for your VIN. Fresh gear oil of the correct type helps many cars. Grinding that keeps getting worse means the synchros need repair.

issues.t: Clutch pedal soft or sticking from master or slave cylinder
issues.sym: The clutch pedal feels spongy, sticks to the floor, or the clutch won't fully release so gears grind or the car creeps. You may see fluid near the pedal or under the car.
issues.why: The hydraulic clutch master and slave cylinders leak or wear out. They are among the most-reported repairs on this car.
issues.next: Check the brake/clutch fluid reservoir. If the pedal stays down or you can't get into gear, don't drive it; have the clutch hydraulics inspected and bled or replaced.

issues.t: Clutch slipping or worn out
issues.sym: Engine revs climb without the car speeding up, a burning smell after hard driving, or a chattering or noisy clutch.
issues.why: The clutch disc, pressure plate, flywheel and release bearing wear out, often around 70,000 to 100,000 miles and sooner with hard launches.
issues.next: Get a quote that includes the flywheel and release bearing. Driving on a slipping clutch can damage the flywheel and raise the bill.

issues.t: Automatic shifter stuck or frozen in cold weather
issues.sym: In snow or freezing weather the automatic shift lever is stiff or won't move, sometimes stuck in Park.
issues.why: Water gets past the boot on the end of the shift cable and freezes. Hyundai ran a service campaign to replace the shift cable boot.
issues.next: Ask a dealer whether the shift cable boot campaign was done on your car. Don't force the lever; let the car warm up.

issues.t: Automatic transmission harsh shifts or failure
issues.sym: Harsh or slow shifts, won't shift out of Park, won't engage when cold, an ESC Off light with transmission codes, or a gear ratio error.
issues.why: Hyundai issued bulletins for transmission software and diagnosis on these cars, and owners report full transmission replacements on both the early 6-speed and later 8-speed automatics.
issues.next: Have the codes read and ask the dealer about software updates. If the transmission won't engage or slips, stop driving it to avoid more damage.

issues.t: Oil leaks from the V6 oil filter housing, timing cover or sensor
issues.sym: Oil spots under the car, a burning-oil smell, or oil on the engine around the oil filter, front cover, back of the engine or the oil pressure sensor.
issues.why: Owners report a cracked oil filter housing, leaking timing chain cover, oil pressure sensor and rear main seal, mostly as the cars age past 80,000 to 100,000 miles.
issues.next: Keep an eye on the oil level and have the leak located. Small leaks can wait a little, but oil dripping onto the exhaust can catch fire.

issues.t: Thermostat failure on the turbo engine
issues.sym: The temperature gauge reads low or swings, the heater blows lukewarm, or a check engine light for engine temperature comes on.
issues.why: The thermostat sticks open or fails. Several turbo owners report replacing it.
issues.next: Have the cooling system checked and the thermostat replaced. If the gauge ever climbs toward hot, pull over and shut the engine off.

issues.t: Coolant leaks and overheating on the V6
issues.sym: Coolant smell, drips under the front of the car, low coolant warnings, or the temperature gauge climbing.
issues.why: On the 2013-2016 V6, owners report water pump failures, thermostat housing leaks and overheating.
issues.next: If the gauge climbs, pull over and shut off the engine. Don't open a hot radiator cap. Have the cooling system pressure-tested.

issues.t: A/C blows warm from compressor or condenser failure
issues.sym: The A/C blows warm, cycles on and off, or makes a whine from the compressor.
issues.why: The A/C compressor and condenser are among the most-reported repairs on this car. Compressor pulley bearings fail, and the low-mounted condenser can be punctured by road debris.
issues.next: Have a shop check for leaks with dye before just recharging. A recharge alone won't last if the condenser or compressor is leaking.

issues.t: Keyless entry door handle button stops working
issues.sym: Pressing the button on the outside door handle no longer locks or unlocks the car, even with the key fob nearby.
issues.why: The touch button and proximity sensor in the door handle fail. This is the most-reported problem in one owner survey; the usual fix is a new door handle.
issues.next: Use the fob buttons or the hidden key in the meantime. A shop or dealer can replace the handle.

issues.t: Brake lights and push-button start fail from brake switch (recall)
issues.sym: The car won't start with the push button, the brake lights don't come on, cruise control won't cancel, or an ESC warning light appears. The shifter may leave Park without pressing the brake.
issues.why: The brake light (stop lamp) switch can malfunction. Hyundai recalled 2010-2011 Genesis Coupes to replace it.
issues.next: Check whether recall 13V113000 has been done. If your brake lights don't work, have it fixed before driving; the dealer replaces the switch free.

issues.t: Passenger airbag sensor connector can come loose (recall)
issues.sym: Usually no warning. The airbag light may come on.
issues.why: The wiring connector for the front passenger seat occupant sensor can work loose when the seat moves. In a crash the passenger airbag would then fire at low power no matter who is sitting there.
issues.next: Look up your VIN for recall 16V722000. The dealer secures the connector free.

issues.t: Rear differential bolts can loosen on manual cars (recall)
issues.sym: Clunking or vibration from the rear, and in the worst case a sudden loss of drive power.
issues.why: On some manual-transmission cars the rear differential was misaligned at the factory, letting its mounting bolts loosen. The driveshaft could then come apart.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 15V756000. If you hear new clunks from the rear, get it inspected before driving further.

issues.t: ABS module can leak and catch fire (recall)
issues.sym: An ABS warning light, a burning smell or smoke from the engine bay, even while the car is parked.
issues.why: Brake fluid can leak inside the ABS control module and short out its circuit board, which can start a fire.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 23V651000. Until it's done, park outside and away from buildings, and stop driving if you smell burning.

issues.t: Car can move if started in gear (recall)
issues.sym: The car lurches when started, without the clutch pressed and with the parking brake off.
issues.why: A return spring in the ignition lock switch can break, so the car can start while in gear.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 24V562000. Until it's done, set the parking brake and shift to neutral before starting.

issues.t: Driver airbag bolts may be loose (recall)
issues.sym: Usually no warning sign.
issues.why: The bolts that hold the driver airbag to the steering wheel may not have been tightened enough, so it could come loose.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 20V248000. The dealer inspects and tightens the bolts free.

issues.t: Water leaks into the tail lights
issues.sym: Fog or water inside the tail light lenses, and sometimes damp carpet in the trunk.
issues.why: The tail light housings and their seals let water in. Owners list it among the most common repairs.
issues.next: Have the seals replaced or the housings resealed. Water in the lights can make bulbs and sockets fail.

issues.t: Weak battery or slow cranking
issues.sym: Slow cranking, a no-start, or an immobilizer warning, especially after the car sits.
issues.why: Several owners report original batteries failing early, plus loose battery cables and grounds.
issues.next: Have the battery and charging system tested and check that the cable clamps are tight.

issues.t: Check engine light from oxygen sensors
issues.sym: Check engine light with oxygen sensor codes, sometimes with slightly worse fuel economy.
issues.why: Oxygen sensors are one of the most-reported failures across both engines.
issues.next: Have the codes read. Replacing the failed sensor usually clears it; check wiring first if codes return.

issues.t: Whining from the serpentine belt idler pulley
issues.sym: A whine or chirp from the front of the engine that changes with engine speed.
issues.why: The bearing in the belt idler or tensioner pulley wears out.
issues.next: Have the pulleys checked and replaced before one seizes and throws the belt.

issues.t: Engine vibration from worn motor mounts
issues.sym: More vibration at idle, clunks when shifting or getting on and off the gas.
issues.why: The engine and transmission mounts wear out.
issues.next: Have a shop check the mounts. Broken mounts can stress hoses and other parts.

issues.t: Radio, navigation or Bluetooth failures
issues.sym: The radio goes silent, the screen goes dark or flickers, Bluetooth won't pair, or satellite radio stops working.
issues.why: Owners report head units and displays failing; some cars were fixed with software updates and others needed a new unit.
issues.next: Ask a dealer about audio software updates before replacing the unit.

issues.t: Paint chipping and clear coat peeling
issues.sym: Lots of chips on the hood and roof, or paint and clear coat peeling on the bumper.
issues.why: Owners report weak paint and failing clear coat on 2013 cars.
issues.next: Document it with photos and ask a Hyundai dealer if any paint coverage applies. Touch up chips early to stop rust.
